entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Kyrillos I (b. 300 CE) was a Christian entrepreneur or business leader of the Roman Empire, active in the Eastern Mediterranean region. He was the founder of the Church of Alexandria, one of the most influential Christian institutions of the time. Kyrillos I played a crucial role in the early Christian Church, serving as the Patriarch of Alexandria from 310 to 337 CE. He was instrumental in the translation of the Bible into Greek and the establishment of the Catechism of the Apostles, which became a standard text for Christian doctrine. Kyrillos I's legacy extends to the development of the Coptic language and the spread of Christianity throughout the Mediterranean world. His impact on the early Christian Church is still felt today, with the Coptic Orthodox Church continuing to thrive in Egypt and other parts of Africa. The Church of Alexandria, which he founded, remains an important center of Christian learning and culture.
